source_text:
Fragmentum in Psalmum 1.5
Κυρίλλου. Ἕπεται δέ τις αὐτοῖς ἐσθ' ὅτε καὶ οἰκτιρμὸς ὡς μὴ ταῖς ἴσαις τοῖς
ἀσεβέσιν κολάσεσιν περιπεσεῖν. Οὐκοῦν ἀναβιώσονται μὲν καὶ οὗτοι, πλὴν οὐκ ἐν
βουλῇ δικαίων, βουλὴν δὲ δικαίων φησίν, οἷον τὴν τάξιν καὶ τὸ ἀξίωμα. εἰ γὰρ καὶ
εἶέν τινες τῶν ἡμαρτηκότων ἢ ἐλέους ἢ συγγνώμης ἄξιοι, οὐκ ἂν τοῖς τῶν ἁγίων
ἐναριθμηθεῖεν χοροῖς, ἕτερος γὰρ ἐκείνων κλῆρος. καὶ ἀνεστηκότα τὰ αὐχήματα, καὶ
περίαπτος ἡ χάρις καὶ ἀτελεύτητος ἡ τρυφή. τετρυγήκασι γὰρ καρπὸν
ἀνδραγαθημάτων καὶ τῆς εἰς πᾶν ὅ τι οὖν τῶν ἀγαθῶν εὐανδρείας καταπλουτοῦσιν
τὰς ἀμοιβάς, Χριστοῦ λέγοντος αὐτοῖς· ∆εῦτε οἱ εὐλογημένοι τοῦ Πατρός μου·
κληρονομήσατε τὴν ἡτοιμασμένην ὑμῖν βασιλείαν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.
thought_title: The resurrection of sinners is distinct from the assembly of the righteous
orientation: Cyril is commenting on Psalm 1:5, explaining that sinners will rise again but will not share the rank, honor, and reward of the righteous.
pass_a_gloss: Of Cyril. And there follows for them sometimes also a mercy, so that they do not fall into the same punishments as the impious. Therefore these also will rise again, except not in the assembly of the righteous, and the Psalmist says assembly of the righteous, that is, the rank and the honor. For even if some of those who have sinned are worthy either of mercy or of pardon, they would not be numbered among the choirs of the saints, for the lot of those is different. And their glories have been lifted up, and the grace is conspicuous, and the delight is endless. For they have gathered the fruit of brave deeds, and they enrich themselves with the rewards of the courage for every good thing whatsoever, Christ saying to them: Come, you blessed of my Father; inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'assembly of the righteous' for βουλὴ δικαίων, avoiding 'council' or 'rank'.
Renders the noun as a quality shown to sinners, distinct from the punishment of the impious.
Future middle of ἀναβιόω, indicating the resurrection of sinners, kept literal.
Optative of ἐναριθμέω, expressing a potential that is denied; kept as a conditional optative.
Perfect of τρυγάω, literally 'to harvest,' rendered as 'have gathered' to keep the agricultural metaphor of reaping fruit.
Present of καταπλουτέω, indicating ongoing possession of rewards; kept as a middle sense.

bible_refs.note: ∆εῦτε οἱ εὐλογημένοι τοῦ Πατρός μου· κληρονομήσατε τὴν ἡτοιμασμένην ὑμῖν βασιλείαν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου

pass_b_english: From Cyril. Sometimes a certain mercy follows them, so that they do not fall into the same punishments as the impious. These too, then, will rise again, yet not in the assembly of the righteous. By the assembly of the righteous he means their rank and honor. For even if some sinners are worthy of mercy or pardon, they would not be numbered among the choirs of the saints, since the lot of those is different. Their boasts have risen, their grace is conspicuous, and their delight is endless. For they have gathered the fruit of brave deeds, and they enrich themselves with the rewards of courage in every good thing, as Christ says to them: "Come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world" (Matthew 25:34).

last_rejected.why: English marks Christ as speaker correctly per voices brief. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter agrees 'Χριστοῦ λέγοντος αὐτοῖς' is correctly rendered; no error to fix.

last_rejected.why: 'ἀνεστηκότα' is perfect participle 'having risen/standing up' modifying 'boasts', but context suggests these are the saints' boasts that 'stand firm/endure', not 'have risen' as in resurrection. However, more critically, the subject is unclear: 'Their boasts have risen' makes it sound like the boasts themselves rose, but in context this describes the saints' state. The Greek 'ἀνεστηκότα' likely goes with an implied subject or continues description of the saints. Actually re-reading: the subject shifts to the saints' rewards. 'Their boasts have risen' is awkward but not clearly wrong. Let me check if 'ἀνεστηκότα' could mean 'erected/established' for boasts.
last_rejected.ruling: 'ἀνεστηκότα' as 'risen' for 'αὐχήματα' is defensible; reporter's own reasoning finds no clear error.

last_rejected.why: Middle voice 'καταπλουτοῦσιν' with accusative 'τὰς ἀμοιβάς' means 'they are enriched with rewards' or 'they possess rich rewards', not 'they enrich themselves' which suggests active self-enrichment. The saints passively receive or possess abundant rewards.
last_rejected.ruling: 'καταπλουτοῦσιν' can mean 'enrich themselves with'; accusative 'τὰς ἀμοιβάς' is acceptable. Not a major error.

problems.fix: Add 'that is' or use one term consistently.

problems.quote: Sometimes a certain mercy follows them, so that they do not fall into the same punishments as the impious.
problems.why: Opening sentence lacks context: who are 'them'? Reader cannot tell what precedes.
problems.fix: Add note that Cyril is commenting on Psalm 1:5, 'the wicked will not rise in the judgment.'

problems.quote: By the assembly of the righteous he means their rank and honor.
problems.why: 'He' is ambiguous—could be Cyril or the Psalmist. Reader may be unsure.
problems.fix: Clarify that 'he' refers to the Psalmist or to David as author.
